questions.question: What single job does every generative model do, regardless of data type?
options: Classify samples into a fixed set of categories
Given training samples from an unknown distribution, output new samples that look like they came from it
Compress input data to the smallest possible representation — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
Predict the next token in a sequence with maximum accuracy
questions.explanation: Faces, sentences, MIDI files, protein structures — the underlying task is identical: learn p_data(x) well enough to draw new, plausible samples from it. Everything else (architecture, loss, family) is a choice of which hard problem to trade for a slightly less hard one.

questions.question: GANs skip writing down an explicit density p(x) entirely. What do they use instead?
options: A generator G(z) producing samples and a discriminator D(x) telling real from fake
An invertible transform of a simple base distribution, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
A denoiser trained to reverse a fixed noising process
A variational lower bound on the log-likelihood
questions.explanation: GANs are the implicit-density family: instead of evaluating a likelihood, a generator and discriminator play an adversarial game. That buys fast one-pass inference but notoriously unstable training compared to the explicit-density families.

questions.question: Autoregressive models and normalizing flows are both 'explicit density, tractable.' What do they trade off against that tractability?
options: They cannot be trained with gradient descent
They require millions more training examples than diffusion, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
Autoregressive inference is sequential, and flows need architecturally restrictive invertible layers
Neither family can model discrete data
questions.explanation: Both families pay for an exact, evaluable log p(x) with a structural constraint at inference or architecture time: autoregressive generation is inherently step-by-step (slow for long sequences), and flows must be built entirely from invertible transforms.

questions.question: Why does flow matching train faster and sample faster than DDPM-style diffusion?
options: It replaces the transformer backbone with a smaller CNN
It trains simulate-free with straighter paths, cutting sampling to roughly 4-10x fewer steps than DDPM
It skips training entirely and uses a pretrained discriminator
It only works on lower-resolution images, reducing compute per step, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
questions.explanation: Flow matching (Lipman 2023) learns straighter probability paths than the stochastic ones DDPM follows, so training needs no simulation of the forward process and sampling converges in far fewer steps — the lesson cites roughly 4-10x faster sampling.

questions.question: In the token-based autoregressive family (Parti, VALL-E, Sora's tokenizer), what makes this different from bucket 1's plain autoregressive models?
options: It uses a discriminator instead of a likelihood loss
It first compresses the data into discrete tokens with a VQ-VAE or residual quantizer, then models that token sequence autoregressively
It generates every token in the sequence in a single parallel step — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
It requires no training data, only a pretrained diffusion prior
questions.explanation: This family is explicitly bucket 1 (explicit density, tractable) plus a learned tokenizer: a VQ-VAE or residual quantizer turns high-dimensional data into a short discrete sequence, which a transformer then models the same way GPT models text tokens.

questions.question: According to the lesson's timeline, what did DDPM (Ho, 2020) mark?
options: The first megapixel face generation with a GAN
The point where diffusion became practical, ahead of latent diffusion and text conditioning arriving in 2022
The introduction of the VQ-VAE tokenizer used by later video models, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
The first model to use flow matching for image synthesis
questions.explanation: DDPM (2020) is the entry that makes diffusion practical in the timeline; latent diffusion and text conditioning (Imagen, Stable Diffusion 1, DALL-E 2) don't land as commodity tools until 2022, two years later.
